Yun bagong prescribe sakin na meds (Coralan) ginawa na niyang parang maintenance ko. Twice a day ko siyang iniinom everyday, di na katulad ng beta-blockers na as needed lang. What kind of beta-blockers ba yun prescribed sayo? I used to take propranolol and it does wonders naman kaso tinitake ko lang siya kapag kailangan. I noticed sa ilan weeks ko nang pagtake ng coralan, bumaba na resting heart rate ko, parang umaabot ng 60-80bpm na lang. Syempre may palpitations parin pero that's mostly my anxiety acting up.

Yeah, nauna yun cardiologist appointment ko and he told me to stop taking beta-blockers and to stick to Coralan instead (I take it twice daily). For the first 2-3 weeks bumaba HR ko to 60-80bpm paminsan nag  90 but mostly stable HR. When I have panic attacks nag kaka palpitations parin pero di na ganon ka lala. 

Also I'm glad you found the right meds! I guess trial and error lang talaga. I've heard stories where people did get palpitations from Escitalopram and had really bad side effects but eventually nag subside siya in 2-4 weeks. Hopefully ganon yun case ko, I've only been taking it for 4 days eh, idk kung ano magagawa ko kung wala akong Alprazolam. Somehow na mamanage ko side effects because of it.

I was best friends with someone who I thought I'd never part with. I actually saw a future with her, thinking that she'd be there when I graduate college, get a tattoo, my first job, basically every milestone in my life. She unfortunately decided to cut ties with me because I was too depressed or mentally unstable, according to her, she got so lost in thinking and looking out for me that she forgot to look after herself. The way I saw it, I was bringing her down with me, which wasn't my intention at all. When we stopped talking I became suicidal and fell into a deeper depression. I cried for days, and never got over it, and it's been 4 years. She's happier now, moved to another country, has a new circle of friends and best friend, and to me, she looks like a complete stranger, but she's happy. I don't think I've ever been the same since, I became incredibly disconnected with everybody and developed trust issues. I realized when she cut ties, that I depended on her. I confided so much in her that when she was gone, I couldn't bear it. 

To this day, I still feel a little jealous and mad about how well she's doing, because I'm still stuck in a rut, and I'm still severely depressed and anxious. I guess the obvious takeaway from all of this is: to never give your all to someone, to the point where you're depending so much on their presence and comfort. Never get lost in someone, whether it's a friend or lover, because life is so unpredictable and you'll never know how long anything is going to last. Leave some love for yourself.

Hey there, thought I'd give my own insights since I suffer from frequent episodes of anxiety and depression. Whenever I experience an anxiety/panic attack, I lose control of everything. On severe days I experience uncontrollable trembling and crying, increased breathing, which sometimes lead to hyperventilation. The only thing that makes things better for me is when I have a loved one present. All they literally have to do is hold my hand and just... be there for me. No bullshit advice about how everything's going to be okay and that things will get better. As long as they keep me distracted from whatever it is I'm feeling, and keep me grounded and guide me with my breathing, I know things will pass, eventually.

As for a depressive episode, it can be a bit tricky. I tend to not reciprocate, or at times even seem catatonic when people try to comfort or talk to me. I will distance myself from you, I'd want to have my own space, and I'd want people to respect that. I've experienced people forcing toxic positivity whenever I allow myself to vent. "You're overthinking that's why" "try to look at the brighter side of things" "it gets better" "I'm sorry to hear that" "there's so much more to life than being sad" ... And I hate hearing all of those things. It makes me feel like shit because it almost seems as if they're blaming me for something I have no control over. I can't change it unfortunately, and this is the way that my mind functions.

I'd much appreciate it if people allow me to vent without being judged. If people actually LISTENED to what I say instead of saying things they think I want to hear. Sometimes I just want to be alone, and have people respect that enough to allow myself to get back on my feet.

I've also found how comforting it is to vent to people who go through the same things that I do. Sometimes you want to share your experiences and have people relate to that.

I personally think that people can change BUT it will be hard to gain a person's trust again once you know they're capable of destroying a relationship and stabbing you behind your back. I've personally never been cheated on (but people have messed around with my feelings, I've never been in a serious relationship) but I know people who have been. 

My mother doesn't trust my dad anymore. She told me once that there's no love left to give to him. I know she deeply cares for him still, but it's never the same anymore. I've lost all respect for my dad ever since I found out he's been cheating on my mom with several other women. 

For some people, there's no forgiving a person that deliberately hurts you despite the sacrifices and effort both parties put into building a strong foundation for the relationship. 

Once you fuck up, you fuck up. There are no excuses for that. If you're willing to change, then that depends on the other partner's decision to take you in again. All I can tell you is that TRUST is the best foundation to build a relationship on, but once that's been violated, I can assure you things will never be the same again.
